<b>Ресничный узел</b> лежит в глазнице с: The ciliary ganglion lies in the orbit beside the optic nerve, about 1 cm from the orbital apex. Its fibers come from the accessory nucleus of nerve III and travel in the nerve itself. Short ciliary nerves carry the signal to the muscle that constricts the pupil and to the ciliary muscle, which adjusts the lens for near vision. Sympathetic fibers pass through the ganglion without synapsing.
<b>Крылонёбный узел</b> — самый крупный: The pterygopalatine ganglion, the largest (3–5 mm), hangs from nerve V₂ behind the maxilla. Fibers from the superior salivatory nucleus run in the facial nerve (VII), leave at the genu as the greater petrosal nerve, and join the nerve of the pterygoid canal. After the ganglion they reach the lacrimal gland (via the zygomatic and lacrimal nerves) and the nasal and palatine glands.
<b>Поднижнечелюстной узел</b> висит на я: The submandibular ganglion hangs from the lingual nerve (V₃) above the gland of the same name. Fibers from the superior salivatory nucleus travel in the facial nerve, through the middle ear as the chorda tympani, and then in the lingual nerve. After the ganglion they go to the submandibular and sublingual glands. The chorda also carries taste from the front two-thirds of the tongue.
<b>Ушной узел</b> лежит под овальным отв: The otic ganglion lies below the foramen ovale, on the inner side of the mandibular nerve (V₃). Fibers from the inferior salivatory nucleus travel in nerve IX: the tympanic nerve rises into the middle ear, forms a plexus there, and leaves as the lesser petrosal nerve. After the ganglion the signal reaches the parotid gland via the auriculotemporal nerve.
<b>Зрачковый рефлекс.</b> Свет на сетчат: Pupillary reflex. Light on the retina → optic nerve → pretectal nuclei of the midbrain → accessory nuclei of III on both sides → ciliary ganglion → the muscle that constricts the pupil. That is why light in one eye constricts both pupils (one side is shown here). In life it takes about 0.2 s. Doctors test the reflex with a penlight: it shows whether the optic nerve, midbrain, and nerve III are intact.
<b>Слюна на еду.</b> Вкус и запах возбуж: Saliva for food. Taste and smell excite the solitary nucleus, and it excites the salivatory nuclei. Saliva flow rises from ≈ 0.3 to 1.5–2 mL/min, and the saliva is watery. At rest the submandibular glands make most of it (≈ 70%), during meals the parotids (≈ 50%). Salivating at the mere sight of food is a conditioned reflex (Pavlov's experiments).
<b>Страх — перевес симпатики.</b> Её вол: Fear — the sympathetic division takes over. Its fibers leave the upper thoracic segments of the spinal cord, synapse in the superior cervical ganglion, and rise as a plexus on the internal carotid artery. Through the orbit (passing through the ciliary ganglion) they reach the muscle that dilates the pupil. The parasympathetic division quiets down: saliva is scant and thick — a dry mouth.
<b>Сдавление нерва III</b> аневризмой за: Compression of nerve III by an aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery or by a brain shifted by swelling. Parasympathetic fibers lie on the surface of the nerve, so the pupil is affected early: it is wide and does not constrict to light. The eyelid droops, and the eye turns down and out. One wide pupil with a severe headache or after head trauma calls for an urgent CT scan.
<b>«Крокодиловы слёзы»</b> (синдром Бого: “Crocodile tears” (Bogorad syndrome). After damage to the facial nerve above the genu, fibers that went to the salivary glands regrow the wrong way — into the greater petrosal nerve, to the pterygopalatine ganglion and the lacrimal gland. Now the eye on the affected side waters while eating. Botulinum toxin injections into the lacrimal gland help.
<b>Синдром Фрея</b> (ушно-височный). Пос: Frey syndrome (auriculotemporal syndrome). After surgery on the parotid gland, its cut fibers grow into the sweat glands and vessels of the cheek skin. Now the cheek flushes and sweats while eating. This is possible because sweat glands also respond to acetylcholine. Botulinum toxin injections into the skin help.
<b>Четыре парасимпатических узла</b> гол: Four parasympathetic ganglia of the head — ciliary, pterygopalatine, submandibular, and otic. In them, fibers from brainstem nuclei carried by nerves III, VII, and IX synapse. The first neuron (thick line) runs from the nucleus to the ganglion, the second (thin) from the ganglion to a muscle or gland along branches of the trigeminal nerve (V). Choose a ganglion.
Зрачок сужается на свет, текут слёзы и с: The pupil narrows in bright light, tears and saliva flow — all without our will. This is run by four small ganglia: fibers from the brainstem synapse in them and reach the eye and glands by borrowing other nerves.
\n <div><h2>Устройство</h2>\n:
Structure

In the head, the parasympathetic division has four pairs of ganglia, and their nuclei lie in the brainstem: the accessory oculomotor nucleus → ciliary ganglion; the superior salivatory nucleus (with the lacrimal nucleus) → via nerve VII to the pterygopalatine and submandibular ganglia; the inferior salivatory nucleus → via nerve IX to the otic ganglion. The vagus nerve (X) is parasympathetic too, but its ganglia lie in the walls of the organs of the neck, chest, and abdomen.

Each ganglion is attached to a branch of the trigeminal nerve. Sensory fibers of V and sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion also pass through it, but only the parasympathetic fibers synapse there.

How it works

In the ganglion the signal is passed on by acetylcholine (nicotinic receptors), and at the muscle or gland also by acetylcholine (muscarinic receptors). The parasympathetic division constricts the pupil and focuses the eye for near vision, triggers tears, abundant watery saliva, and secretion of the nasal glands. The sympathetic division acts on the same organs by its own routes: it dilates the pupil and constricts the vessels of the glands.

Medicine

  • Atropine blocks muscarinic receptors: eye drops dilate the pupil for examining the fundus and temporarily abolish accommodation; pills with a similar action often cause a dry mouth.
  • Pilocarpine does the opposite: it constricts the pupil (a glaucoma treatment) and increases salivation in dry mouth.
  • Adie's tonic pupil is damage to the ciliary ganglion, often after a viral infection: the pupil is wide, barely reacts to light, and slowly constricts when looking at something near.
  • Horner syndrome is damage to the sympathetic pathway: a small pupil, a drooping eyelid, and dry skin on half of the face.
  • Sjögren syndrome is autoimmune damage to the lacrimal and salivary glands: dry eyes and a dry mouth.

Simplifications

  • The right side of the head is shown. Nerves are drawn thicker than in life, and the ganglia are enlarged (in reality 2–5 mm); the course of nerves in bony canals is simplified. The sensory roots of the ganglia and the sympathetic plexus of the external carotid artery are not shown. Reflexes are slowed down: in life they take fractions of a second. The round “pupil” window shows the same eye from the front, enlarged; it always faces you.
